issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Rideable.messageOnRide() to be a no-argument method returning a String (UML and example in the problem show messageOnRide():String and Main calls r.messageOnRide()). However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (a method with one String parameter) and implements Pig and Seal accordingly. This parameter mismatch between the specification/template and the solution will confuse students about the correct method signature and can lead to compilation errors if students follow the problem statement or the template Main usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the problem/template by defining Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"; or (B) Update the problem statement, UML, and template Main usage to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and document the equipment parameter so all artifacts agree. Option A is recommended to match the current problem description and template usage.

issues.description: The Problem Statement and template expect a parameterless method messageOnRide() on the Rideable interface (and call r.messageOnRide() in Main), but the Solution Repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it in Pig and Seal with an extra 'equipment' parameter and a different return format. This naming/signature mismatch breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description and template to the solution: students following the template or the problem text will attempt to call a parameterless method and expect the return 'Riding on [Animal Type] [name]', while the solution requires an argument and returns 'Riding on [Type] [name] with [equipment]'.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API across artifacts by using a parameterless messageOnRide() method. Specifically, change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning the expected string format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if the equipment parameter is intentional, update the Problem Statement and template Main.java to call messageOnRide(String) and document the parameter; however, the simpler fix is to remove the extra 'equipment' parameter in the solution so it matches the exercise description.
